newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea First Bank has no liquidity problem-BOK.
newsitem.headline: Korea First Bank has no liquidity problem-BOK.

text.p: Korea First Bank faces no liquidity problem despite the collapse of Sammi Steel Co, a senior central Bank of Korea (BOK) official said on Thursday.
Korea First is Sammi Steel's major creditor.

"The Korea First Bank has no funding problem at all despite Sammi," Park Chul, head of the central bank's monetary policy department, told Reuters. "As it is one of the nation's biggest banks, it can handle the Sammi case."
Park denied local media reports that the central bank planned to extend emergency loans to Korea First to help ease liquiditiy problems.

Sammi Steel, South Korea's largest stainless steel producer, defaulted on 1.8 billion won worth of promissory notes and all local banks on Thursday froze checking accounts with the company. It has filed for court receivership.
"We are not considering granting any emergency loans to Korea First Bank at all," Park said.
He said Korea First could utilise the call money market if necessary. "The nation's call money market is large with its trading volume totalling nine to 10 trillion won a day."
Korea First Bank had 217.4 billion won of outstanding loans to Sammi Steel as of Monday, down from 395.9 billion at the end of 1996, a bank spokesman said.
The European rating agency IBCA said on Wednesday it had downgraded the individual ratings of Korea First Bank (KFB), Cho Hung Bank and Korea Exchange Bank (KEB).
"KFB's individual rating has been downgraded to D/E from C/D. Both Cho Hung and KEB have been downgraded to C/D from C," IBCA said.
IBCA said it planned to make a detailed analysis of the impact of the Sammi failure in its annual review of Korean banks in April.
